statement: You are given an array nums in which no two adjacent elements are equal. A peak is an element that is strictly greater than each of its neighbours.
Treat the positions just outside the array as −∞, so nums[0] only needs to beat nums[1], and nums[n − 1] only needs to beat nums[n − 2].

Return the index of a peak. If the array has several peaks, the index of any one of them is accepted. The search must run in O(log n) time: if nums[mid] < nums[mid + 1], the values rise to the right and a peak must exist there; otherwise one exists at mid or to its left.

examples.explanation: nums[2] = 3 is greater than both 2 and 1, so index 2 is a peak.
nums[5] = 6 is greater than 5 and 4, so index 5 is a peak. Index 1 (value 2) is also a peak, and either answer would be accepted.
The values only fall, so the only peak is the first element: 5 beats its single neighbour 4 and the −∞ on its left.

constraints: nums[i] ≠ nums[i + 1] for every valid i
